package.title: 100 HEC LAT-Style Critical Reasoning MCQs with Explanations

questions.question: A town installed brighter streetlights on several roads, and reported night-time thefts later fell on those roads. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Brighter lights may have contributed to the decline in reported thefts.
Every road in the town is now safer.
Theft has ended because of the new lights.
Residents no longer report theft at night.

questions.question: A college claims its new study room improves examination results because students who used it scored higher than those who did not. What is the central weakness?
choices: The users may already have been more motivated or better prepared.
Examination results cannot be compared between students.
A study room cannot be used by more than one student.
The claim does not say what colour the room is.

questions.question: A library extended its opening hours. The manager concludes that more people will borrow books. Which assumption is necessary?
choices: Some potential borrowers can use the library during the added hours.
Every visitor prefers printed books to digital books.
The library will purchase a new building.
Borrowing books is the only reason people visit.

questions.question: A report says that all applicants who met the stated minimum requirement were considered for interview. Sana met that requirement. What follows?
choices: Sana was considered for interview.
Sana was selected for the job.
Sana performed better than every other applicant.
Sana accepted an interview invitation.

questions.question: A shop owner argues that lowering prices increased sales because more units were sold in the week after the reduction. Which information would most weaken the argument?
choices: The week after the reduction included a major festival absent from the comparison week.
The shop displayed the lower prices clearly.
Some customers paid in cash.
The shop sells several different products.

questions.question: A school says that its new reading programme caused improved reading scores. Which evidence would strengthen the claim most?
choices: Comparable pupils assigned to the programme improved more than pupils not assigned to it.
The programme uses colourful books.
Teachers say that reading is important.
The school also repainted its classrooms.

questions.question: A survey of 30 volunteers at a fitness centre finds that most support a new exercise policy. The organiser concludes that most residents support it. What is the main flaw?
choices: The volunteers may not represent residents generally.
The policy is necessarily unpopular with fitness-centre members.
A survey can never provide useful information.
The organiser has not stated the policy's cost.

questions.question: A bus route carried more passengers after its timetable was made more frequent. Which conclusion is most careful?
choices: The more frequent timetable may have helped attract passengers.
The timetable was the sole reason passenger numbers rose.
Every passenger prefers frequent buses.
The route is now profitable.

questions.question: A manager says, 'Our office should adopt paperless forms because printing costs will fall.' Which assumption best supports the reasoning?
choices: The cost of adopting and maintaining the system will not outweigh the printing savings.
Every employee already owns a printer.
Paper forms are always inaccurate.
No client will ever need assistance.

questions.question: A notice states that the clinic is closed on Sundays and open on every other day. Which statement follows?
choices: The clinic is open on Saturday.
The clinic is open every Sunday morning.
The clinic closes whenever it is busy.
The clinic is open only on weekdays.

questions.question: A company claims that its training course reduces workplace errors because error reports fell after the course began. What additional fact most weakens the claim?
choices: The company also introduced a rule discouraging employees from reporting minor errors.
The course included practical demonstrations.
Employees received the course during working hours.
The company sells products in several regions.

questions.question: A researcher finds that neighbourhoods with more trees tend to have lower summer temperatures. What can be inferred?
choices: Tree-rich neighbourhoods in the study tended to have lower summer temperatures.
Planting one tree will lower any home's temperature by a fixed amount.
Trees are the only factor affecting neighbourhood temperature.
Every neighbourhood with few trees has a high temperature.

questions.question: An argument says: 'The town should repair the footpath because many pedestrians currently avoid it.' Which assumption connects the evidence to the recommendation?
choices: Repairing the footpath would make it more usable for pedestrians.
Every pedestrian owns a bicycle.
The town has no roads.
Avoiding the footpath is illegal.

questions.question: A student concludes that a particular book is easy because two classmates found it easy. Which fact would most challenge this conclusion?
choices: The classmates had already studied the book's subject in depth.
The book has a blue cover.
The student borrowed the book from a library.
The classmates read it in different rooms.

questions.question: Every member of a committee must sign the final report. Amir signed the final report. What can be concluded?
choices: Amir is a committee member.
Amir may be a committee member, but the statement does not establish that he is.
Only committee members can sign the report.
Amir wrote the entire report.

questions.question: A restaurant claims a new menu improved customer satisfaction because positive comments increased. Which evidence would most strengthen the claim?
choices: A comparable customer survey shows satisfaction rose after the menu change.
The menu uses a larger font.
The restaurant opened a second branch.
The chef has worked there for many years.

questions.question: A school has fewer late arrivals since it began sending reminder messages. Which alternative explanation most weakens the claim that reminders caused the decline?
choices: The school also changed its first-period start time to later in the morning.
The messages were sent by phone.
Some pupils read the messages at home.
The school records arrival times.

questions.question: A report says that no applicant without a completed form can be assessed. Bilal's form is incomplete. What follows?
choices: Bilal cannot be assessed.
Bilal will be rejected permanently.
Bilal did not submit any documents.
Bilal's form contains incorrect information.

questions.question: A newspaper argues that a city should add bicycle lanes because many residents cycle. Which fact most weakens the argument?
choices: The proposed lanes would remove the only safe route for emergency vehicles.
Some residents own bicycles.
Cycling can provide exercise.
The city has several parks.

questions.question: A shop sells a product for less than a nearby shop. Which conclusion is justified by that information alone?
choices: Its listed price for that product is lower than the nearby shop's.
Its product is better quality.
It has lower operating costs.
All its products are cheaper.

questions.question: A council argues that adding more rubbish bins will reduce litter. Which assumption is necessary?
choices: A meaningful amount of litter is caused by a lack of convenient disposal places.
Every resident produces the same amount of rubbish.
The bins will be made from recycled material.
Litter is the only problem in the area.

questions.question: A report finds that students who sleep longer often earn higher marks. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Longer sleep is associated with higher marks among the students studied.
Sleeping longer guarantees higher marks for every student.
High marks always cause students to sleep longer.
Sleep has no relation to academic performance.

questions.question: A coach claims that a new warm-up routine prevents injuries because no team member was injured in the first week. What is the strongest criticism?
choices: One injury-free week is too little evidence to establish prevention.
Warm-ups must always cause injuries.
The team should stop all physical activity.
The routine is ineffective because it is new.

questions.question: If a proposal is approved, the committee will publish it. The committee published the proposal. What can be concluded?
choices: The proposal was approved.
The proposal may have been approved, but publication alone does not prove it.
The committee did not approve the proposal.
Only approved proposals can ever be published.

questions.question: A town's recycling rate rose after it introduced separate collection bins. Which evidence most strengthens the claim that the bins helped?
choices: Similar nearby towns without new bins did not show a comparable rise during the same period.
The bins are painted different colours.
The town held a sports event that month.
Residents can see the bins from the main road.

questions.question: A lecturer says, 'The library is quiet, so it is the best place for every student to study.' Which flaw is clearest?
choices: It assumes that quietness is the only feature relevant to every student's study needs.
It proves that the library is noisy.
It confuses students with lecturers.
It gives a precise count of library users.

questions.question: A report states that some city residents work from home. Which statement must be true?
choices: At least one city resident works from home.
Most city residents work from home.
No city resident travels to work.
Every city resident can work from home.

questions.question: A company claims its new packaging is environmentally preferable because it uses less plastic. Which information most weakens the claim?
choices: Producing the replacement material causes substantially greater environmental harm.
The package is smaller than before.
Customers can open it easily.
The company sells the product online.

questions.question: All candidates who pass the written stage may attend the next stage. Nadia passed the written stage. What follows?
choices: Nadia may attend the next stage.
Nadia must pass the next stage.
Nadia has been appointed.
Only Nadia passed the written stage.

questions.question: A shopkeeper says a new sign increased customers because more people entered after it was installed. Which question would be most useful to evaluate the claim?
choices: Did customer numbers also rise at similar shops without new signs during that period?
What material was used to make the sign?
How many colours are on the sign?
Does the shopkeeper prefer large signs?

questions.question: A school proposes replacing some lectures with recorded lessons, arguing that this will save classroom time. Which assumption is needed?
choices: Students can access and use the recordings for the lessons being replaced.
Every student owns the same device.
Classrooms will no longer be needed.
Recorded lessons are always shorter than lectures.

questions.question: A survey finds that residents who use a park report greater wellbeing than residents who do not. Which fact most challenges a claim that park use causes wellbeing?
choices: People with greater wellbeing may be more likely to visit parks.
The park has several walking paths.
The survey asked about wellbeing.
Some residents live near the park.

questions.question: A student says, 'The last two novels I read by this author were excellent, so every novel by the author is excellent.' What is the main flaw?
choices: It generalizes about all the author's novels from only two examples.
It assumes novels have authors.
It compares novels with non-fiction books.
It concludes that the two novels were not excellent.

questions.question: The museum is free on the first Monday of each month. Today is the first Monday of the month. What follows?
choices: Admission today is free.
Admission is free every Monday.
The museum is open every day.
Every visitor must reserve a place.

questions.question: A business argues that it should offer flexible hours because employees say they find commuting difficult. Which additional evidence would strengthen the argument?
choices: Employees with flexible hours have fewer attendance problems than comparable employees without them.
The office has a large meeting room.
Some employees commute by bus.
The business has operated for ten years.

questions.question: A researcher concludes that a new tutoring service raised scores because users improved more than before. Which fact most weakens that conclusion?
choices: The users were selected because their scores had been unusually low on the first test.
The tutoring sessions covered the tested subject.
The tutor kept attendance records.
The second test used the same scoring scale.

questions.question: A rule states that only registered members may borrow equipment. Zoya borrowed equipment. What follows?
choices: Zoya is a registered member.
Zoya borrowed it without permission.
Every registered member borrowed equipment.
Zoya owns the equipment.

questions.question: A restaurant concludes that its food is more popular because it sold more meals this month than last month. Which information most weakens the conclusion?
choices: The restaurant was open for twice as many days this month.
The restaurant changed the colour of its menu.
The meals were served on plates.
Some customers paid by card.

questions.question: A report says no trained driver in the sample had a collision during the observation period. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: No trained driver in that sample had a collision during that period.
Training prevents every collision.
Untrained drivers always have collisions.
The sample represents all drivers.

questions.question: A council claims that adding a public water fountain will reduce plastic bottle waste. Which assumption is necessary?
choices: Some people who would otherwise use disposable bottles will use the fountain instead.
Every resident carries a reusable bottle.
Plastic bottles are never recycled.
The fountain will be placed indoors.

questions.question: A writer states: 'The proposal has not been rejected, so it must have been accepted.' What is the flaw?
choices: It treats two possibilities as exhaustive even though the proposal could still be pending.
It assumes that proposals can be discussed.
It confuses a writer with a reader.
It gives evidence that the proposal was rejected.

questions.question: A college says a new advising service improved retention because more students returned the following year. What evidence would most strengthen its claim?
choices: Comparable students offered the service returned at a higher rate than those not offered it.
The service uses a newly decorated office.
The college added more courses that year.
Students can book appointments online.

questions.question: A report says that most applicants submitted their forms online. Which statement follows?
choices: More than half of the applicants submitted their forms online.
Every applicant submitted a form online.
Exactly half submitted forms online.
No applicant submitted a paper form.

questions.question: A school claims that a quiet-room policy improves concentration because pupils in the room completed more tasks. Which fact would most weaken the claim?
choices: The pupils using the room were given easier tasks than other pupils.
The room has fewer distractions.
Pupils worked individually in the room.
Teachers recorded completed tasks.

questions.question: If the office receives a complete application, it sends a confirmation email. Farah received a confirmation email. What can be concluded?
choices: Farah may have submitted a complete application, but the email alone does not prove it.
Farah definitely submitted an incomplete application.
The office never sends confirmation emails.
Only Farah received an email.

questions.question: A company says its new delivery system is faster because one order arrived earlier than expected. What is the strongest criticism?
choices: One order does not establish the system's typical delivery speed.
An order cannot arrive early.
The company should stop delivering orders.
Customers always prefer slower delivery.

questions.question: A community group argues that a vacant lot should become a playground because children in the area have few places to play. Which assumption is most important?
choices: The lot can be made safe and suitable for children's play.
All children prefer outdoor games.
The lot is the largest land parcel in the district.
No adult uses the area.

questions.question: An analyst notes that a city's electricity use fell during a mild winter and concludes that insulation upgrades caused the decrease. Which fact most weakens the conclusion?
choices: Residents needed less heating during the mild winter.
Some buildings were upgraded with insulation.
The city records electricity use monthly.
The upgrades were completed before winter.

questions.question: All books in the display are available for loan. This book is in the display. What follows?
choices: This book is available for loan.
This book has already been borrowed.
Only displayed books can be borrowed.
Every book in the library is displayed.

questions.question: A survey finds that people who eat breakfast report better concentration. Which conclusion is most cautious?
choices: Breakfast eating is associated with better reported concentration in the survey.
Breakfast guarantees concentration for everyone.
Poor concentration causes people to eat breakfast.
The survey proves breakfast has no effect.

questions.question: A manager claims that a shorter meeting format saves staff time. Which fact most weakens the claim?
choices: The shorter meetings require lengthy follow-up meetings to resolve unfinished issues.
The meetings begin on time.
Staff receive agendas in advance.
The office has a shared calendar.

questions.question: A school says that its attendance improved after it began calling absent pupils' families. Which question best tests whether the calls caused the improvement?
choices: Did comparable schools without the calling policy show a similar attendance increase?
What brand of phone did the school use?
How many teachers work at the school?
Were the calls made in the morning?

questions.question: A critic argues that a public garden is unnecessary because the district already has a sports field. What is the main weakness?
choices: It assumes a sports field meets the same needs as a public garden.
It proves that the district has no residents.
It assumes gardens contain plants.
It establishes that the sports field is always open.

questions.question: A rule says that a person may enter the laboratory only if wearing safety glasses. Hamza entered the laboratory. What follows?
choices: Hamza was wearing safety glasses.
Hamza works in the laboratory.
Everyone wearing safety glasses entered.
Hamza used every laboratory instrument.

questions.question: A firm claims its customer-support change reduced complaints because complaint numbers fell. Which additional information would most weaken the claim?
choices: The firm made it harder for customers to submit complaints.
The support team now answers calls more quickly.
The firm sells fewer product types than before.
Customers can contact support by email.

questions.question: A library's new online catalogue is used by more patrons than the old catalogue was. Which claim is supported?
choices: More patrons used the new catalogue than used the old one.
The new catalogue is easier for every patron.
The new catalogue caused more people to visit the library.
The old catalogue contained incorrect information.

questions.question: A town proposes a late-night bus service because some workers finish shifts after the current buses stop. Which assumption best supports the proposal?
choices: Some of those workers would use the late-night service.
All workers prefer travelling by bus.
The current buses are always full.
Every employer operates at night.

questions.question: A researcher reports that students who attend every class score higher on average. What is one plausible alternative explanation?
choices: Students with stronger prior preparation may both attend more and score higher.
Scores are always unrelated to learning.
Attending class is impossible for students.
Every student takes a different subject.

questions.question: A proposal is popular among people who attended a public meeting. The organiser concludes that it is popular across the whole district. What is the main concern?
choices: Meeting attendees may not represent the district's residents.
The proposal must be unpopular with attendees.
Public meetings cannot include opinions.
The district has no residents who work.

questions.question: A claim says that all items stored in Cabinet A are labelled. One labelled item is found on a desk. What can be concluded?
choices: The item is not shown to have come from Cabinet A.
The item definitely came from Cabinet A.
The item is unlabelled.
Nothing stored in Cabinet A is labelled.

questions.question: A school argues that a new library will improve learning because students will have more books available. Which evidence most strengthens the argument?
choices: Comparable students with access to the new library use its resources and improve on relevant learning measures.
The library's walls are newly painted.
The school has a large playground.
Some students enjoy reading at home.

questions.question: A news report says that a medicine helped some patients in a small study. Which conclusion goes beyond the evidence?
choices: The medicine will help every patient who takes it.
Some patients in the study improved after receiving it.
The study offers preliminary information about the medicine.
Further evidence could clarify its effects.

questions.question: An office introduces a four-day workweek and reports that output per employee rose. Which information would most weaken the claim that the new schedule caused the rise?
choices: The office also installed software that automated a large share of routine work.
Employees liked having an extra day off.
The office recorded output before and after the change.
Some employees work from home.

questions.question: If a file is confidential, it must be stored in the secure cabinet. This file is stored in the secure cabinet. What follows?
choices: The file might be confidential, but its storage alone does not prove that it is.
The file is definitely not confidential.
Only confidential files are stored in the cabinet.
The file has been read by the whole office.

questions.question: A shop says its loyalty scheme increased sales because members spent more than non-members. Which fact most challenges the conclusion?
choices: The scheme attracted customers who were already frequent, high-spending shoppers.
Members received a card.
The shop sells groceries.
Some non-members visited the shop.

questions.question: A report states that a new bridge is used by both pedestrians and cyclists. Which statement must be true?
choices: At least one pedestrian and at least one cyclist use the bridge.
Most bridge users are cyclists.
No vehicles use the bridge.
Every pedestrian also cycles.

questions.question: A neighbourhood group argues that a vacant shop should become a clinic because residents travel far for basic care. What evidence would most strengthen the proposal?
choices: A needs assessment finds enough local demand and confirms the shop can be adapted for clinical use.
The shop has a wide front window.
Some residents own cars.
The neighbourhood has several restaurants.

questions.question: A student says, 'I revised for one hour and passed, so one hour of revision is enough for every student.' What is the main flaw?
choices: It generalizes from one student's experience to all students.
It assumes passing is possible.
It confuses revision with examination.
It proves that one hour is never useful.

questions.question: Every approved expense has a receipt attached. An expense has no receipt attached. What follows?
choices: The expense is not shown to be approved.
The expense must be approved.
The receipt was lost after approval.
No expenses are approved.

questions.question: A city says traffic congestion fell after it introduced a toll. Which information most weakens the claim that the toll caused the decline?
choices: A major road was closed for repairs during the same period.
The toll amount was posted clearly.
Some drivers paid electronically.
The city has several traffic lights.

questions.question: A committee recommends translating a public notice because many residents speak another language. Which assumption is most important?
choices: A translated notice would help some residents understand the information.
Every resident speaks only one language.
The notice is already difficult for officials to read.
The committee can eliminate every communication problem.

questions.question: A company reports that staff satisfaction rose after it introduced a recognition scheme. Which further information would most strengthen a causal interpretation?
choices: Comparable staff groups without the scheme did not show a similar rise.
The scheme uses certificates.
The company has several departments.
Managers announced the scheme by email.

questions.question: A guide says that every express train stops at Central Station. Train X stops at Central Station. What follows?
choices: Train X may be express, but the stop alone does not establish that it is.
Train X is not express.
Only express trains stop at Central Station.
Train X stops at every station.

questions.question: A school claims that offering free breakfast improves attendance because attendance rose after the programme began. Which fact most weakens the claim?
choices: The school also changed its attendance recording system so fewer absences were counted.
Breakfast is served before classes.
Pupils can choose from several foods.
The programme began at the start of a term.

questions.question: A report says that a policy reduced waiting time at one clinic. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: Waiting time fell at that clinic after the policy was applied, according to the report.
The policy will reduce waiting time at every clinic.
Every patient received immediate care.
The clinic no longer needs staff.

questions.question: A manager says employees should receive written instructions because verbal instructions are sometimes forgotten. Which assumption supports the recommendation?
choices: Employees can consult written instructions when they need to remember the task.
All verbal instructions are incorrect.
Employees never read documents.
Written instructions eliminate every workplace error.

questions.question: A researcher finds that people who use a certain app exercise more often. Which fact most weakens the inference that the app causes more exercise?
choices: The app is marketed mainly to people who already exercise regularly.
The app records exercise sessions.
Some users exercise outdoors.
The app is available on several phones.

questions.question: A local council says that replacing old street signs will reduce navigation errors. Which assumption is necessary?
choices: Some navigation errors occur because the old signs are unclear or difficult to read.
Every traveller uses a paper map.
The new signs will be larger than every building.
Navigation errors are the only cause of late arrivals.

questions.question: A reader claims a newspaper is unbiased because it published criticism of both major parties. Which fact most challenges the claim?
choices: It published substantially more favourable coverage of one party than the other.
It publishes news every day.
Its articles have headlines.
Readers can access it online.

questions.question: If a candidate submits the required documents, the application is complete. This application is complete. What can be concluded?
choices: The candidate may have submitted the required documents, but completeness alone does not prove it.
The candidate submitted no documents.
Only complete applications are ever reviewed.
The application must be incomplete.

questions.question: A library reports more visits after adding weekend hours. Which evidence would most weaken the claim that the new hours caused the rise?
choices: A nearby event brought unusually large crowds to the library during the same period.
The library kept a record of visits.
Weekend hours were announced in advance.
Some visitors borrowed books.

questions.question: A report says that no participant who completed the course failed the final assessment. Which conclusion is warranted?
choices: In the reported group, course completers did not fail the final assessment.
Completing the course guarantees success for every future participant.
Every participant completed the course.
Participants who failed did not attend any classes.

questions.question: A business proposes a self-service checkout to reduce queues. Which assumption is most important?
choices: Some customers will use the self-service checkout instead of waiting for a staffed checkout.
All customers prefer shopping without staff.
The store has no other queues.
Every purchase contains exactly one item.

questions.question: An author argues that a town should preserve an old building because it is historically significant. Which fact most strengthens the argument?
choices: Independent records show that the building is associated with an important event in the town's history.
The building has several windows.
The building is near a bus stop.
Some residents prefer modern architecture.

questions.question: A school reports fewer disciplinary incidents after introducing a new rule. Which evidence most weakens the claim that behaviour improved?
choices: The school stopped recording minor incidents after the rule was introduced.
Teachers explained the rule to pupils.
The rule applies in classrooms.
Some incidents still occurred.

questions.question: A notice states that the training room is reserved for registered participants. A person is not registered. What follows?
choices: The person is not entitled to use the room under the stated reservation rule.
The person has attended the training before.
The person is registered under another name.
The room is empty.

questions.question: A company says that a new product is reliable because one customer used it for a year without a problem. What is the main weakness?
choices: One customer's experience is too limited to establish reliability generally.
A product cannot be used for a year.
The customer must have used the product incorrectly.
Reliability has no meaning for products.

questions.question: A council argues that adding shade at a bus stop will make waiting more comfortable. Which assumption is required?
choices: Exposure to sun or weather currently makes waiting less comfortable for some passengers.
All passengers wait for the same bus.
The bus stop is the only public space nearby.
Shade will make buses arrive sooner.

questions.question: A report finds that districts with more public parks have lower rates of reported stress. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: The districts studied show an association between more parks and lower reported stress.
Building one park will eliminate stress in any district.
Parks are the only cause of stress levels.
People with stress never use parks.

questions.question: A manager claims that a new checklist reduced packing errors because fewer errors were found. Which question is most important?
choices: Was the method for detecting and recording errors kept the same?
What colour is the checklist?
How many employees work in the office?
Does the checklist have a title?

questions.question: Only staff with a current permit may operate the machine. Leena has a current permit. What follows?
choices: Leena is allowed to operate the machine under the stated rule.
Leena must operate the machine today.
Everyone with a permit operates the machine.
Leena has trained every staff member.

questions.question: A town claims a new recycling campaign increased recycling because the amount collected rose. Which fact most weakens the claim?
choices: A nearby recycling facility began accepting materials that were previously excluded.
The campaign used posters.
Residents received collection calendars.
The town weighed collected materials.

questions.question: A report says that some applicants who were interviewed received offers. Which statement must be true?
choices: At least one interviewed applicant received an offer.
Every interviewed applicant received an offer.
No applicant received an offer without an interview.
Most applicants were interviewed.

questions.question: A college says an online appointment system reduced missed appointments because the recorded number of missed appointments fell. Which information most weakens the claim?
choices: The college reduced the number of appointments available during the same period.
Students can book appointments online.
The system sends reminders.
Staff record appointment outcomes.

questions.question: A newspaper argues that a public meeting should be held in the evening because many residents work during the day. Which assumption best supports the argument?
choices: Some residents who cannot attend during the day would be able to attend in the evening.
Every resident works the same hours.
The meeting will be held outdoors.
Daytime meetings are always shorter.

questions.question: A claim says that a new reading app improved vocabulary because users learned more words than before. Which evidence most strengthens the claim?
choices: A comparable group not using the app showed less improvement on the same vocabulary measure.
The app includes animated pictures.
Users can change the background colour.
The app can be downloaded on phones.

questions.question: A person argues, 'The town's new policy is effective because no one has complained about it.' What is the main flaw?
choices: Absence of complaints does not establish that the policy is effective.
An effective policy must receive many complaints.
The town cannot have policies.
People complain only when policies are effective.

questions.question: A school states that students who submit every assignment are eligible for a certificate. Rafi submitted every assignment. What follows?
choices: Rafi is eligible for a certificate.
Rafi has received the certificate.
Rafi earned the highest score.
Only Rafi submitted every assignment.

questions.question: A district plans to add signs directing visitors to a clinic, arguing that this will reduce missed appointments. Which assumption is most important?
choices: Some missed appointments occur because visitors have difficulty finding the clinic.
Every visitor arrives by car.
The clinic has no appointment system.
Signs will shorten the medical consultation.

questions.question: A researcher observes that homes with solar panels have lower electricity bills. Which fact most weakens the claim that panels caused the lower bills?
choices: Panel owners also tend to use less electricity than other households.
Solar panels are installed on roofs.
Some households receive monthly bills.
The study includes several homes.

choices: At least one interviewed applicant received an offer.
Every interviewed applicant received an offer.
No applicant received an offer without an interview.
Most applicants were interviewed.

questions.question: A school has fewer late arrivals since it began sending reminder messages. Which alternative explanation most weakens the claim that reminders caused the decline?
choices: The school also changed its first-period start time to later in the morning.
The messages were sent by phone.
Some pupils read the messages at home.
The school records arrival times.

questions.question: A student says, 'The last two novels I read by this author were excellent, so every novel by the author is excellent.' What is the main flaw?

It assumes novels have authors.
It compares novels with non-fiction books.
It concludes that the two novels were not excellent.

questions.question: A town claims a new recycling campaign increased recycling because the amount collected rose. Which fact most weakens the claim?
choices: A nearby recycling facility began accepting materials that were previously excluded.
The campaign used posters.
Residents received collection calendars.
The town weighed collected materials.
